items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: And once I discovered that Louis Armstrong was the greatest, I never changed my opinion, he still is the greatest.

ctx.x: Was there a particular reason that you were more attracted to the quote classic jazz than bop?

Well I don’t know quite how to answer that. My first love was of course the big bands and by the early ‘40s I was fairly sophisticated in my tastes. I loved Ellington, Goodman, Artie Shaw. I was realizing that there were the “hot” swing bands and then there was more commercial bands. By that time I had listened to Glenn Miller for a couple of years and he was a little too commercial for my taste. I was quite bored with “In the Mood” by then. But my discovery of earlier jazz really was because the big companies,…
You felt that their music was kind of introverted, more towards just for the musician?

items.title: Bob Wilber Interview, 1961-05-01
items.q: I think that was the reason I became a musician, was Louis Armstrong's not fine.

ctx.x: About 1940, yeah. And I remember my first impression of this music, the Muskrat Ramble and Yes, I'm in the Barrel and all those wonderful things, it made no sense to me whatsoever. I was used to the big band riffs and there was no, the melodies were much too complex for me to understand. But I stuck with it and got to love the music. And I think that was the reason I became a musician, was Louis Armstrong's not fine.
